solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Iconic scene fit possibly for a type of literature

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the three words before it may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A recognisable film or book scene might suit a particular literary genre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ICONIC SCENE FIT, all fourteen letters, with 'for' joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This genre of speculative fiction is one kind of literature, imagining future technology and worlds.

clue.text: Some hero symbolised in noted statue

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A heroic figure is represented in a famous piece of sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in noted statue' as the definition; 'in' is only a link word joining the wordplay to 'noted statue'. 'Some' takes letters from hERO Symbolised. Eros is the famous statue at Piccadilly Circus in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure atop the Shaftesbury Memorial in Piccadilly Circus, London, is popularly called by this name and is a famous sculpture.

clue.text: Equipment close to table for flying item

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so this picks the end of table

explanation.surface: Some gear placed near a table is meant for an aircraft or something that flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near' but takes the last letter of 'table'.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy on a string flown in the wind is an item that flies.

clue.text: Fish enjoyed overlooking quay

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: to have had something can mean to have enjoyed it, as in had a good time
a dock is a quay where ships berth

explanation.surface: Someone liked the seafood while gazing over the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic food fish of the cod family, a staple of British fish and chips.

clue.text: Merchant's partner close to bust, one in debt in retreat

parts.note: James Ivory was film-making partner of producer Ismail Merchant in Merchant Ivory Productions

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, so the end of bust is taken

parts.note: someone who owes money is an ower

explanation.surface: A trader's associate is near ruin, a debtor fleeing the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant' is capitalised at the start to hide that it is a name: Merchant Ivory made films such as A Room with a View. 'close to' takes T from 'bust'; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of seclusion from the practical world, especially for academics, is a retreat in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Attraction supplied by game in feature of castle?

parts.note: a draw is something that attracts people, as in the star was a big draw
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A tourist attraction is provided by a game played inside a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied by' and 'in' are only link words; the question mark admits the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged bridge over a moat that can be raised is a typical part of a medieval castle.

clue.text: Lucid narrative representing justice say

indicators.note: representing here means presenting again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clear story that portrays justice, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representing' rearranges LUCID NARRATIVE; 'say' marks justice as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice is one of the four classical moral excellences, alongside prudence, temperance and fortitude.

clue.text: Lousy and ill-fitting caftan? It's yours

indicators.note: something ill-fitting is out of shape, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone is told their baggy robe is shoddy and doesn't fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-fitting' rearranges CAFTAN ITS YOURS; 'and' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lousy is slang for poor in quality, which matches something not good enough.

clue.text: Reformed faculty member grabbing second broadcaster

parts.note: something reformed is made new
a reader is a senior university teacher in Britain, a member of a faculty

explanation.surface: A changed academic who seized a moment became a presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a reader ranks just below a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads the news on radio or television is a broadcaster.

clue.text: English port and whisky

definitions.meaning: a historic Cinque Port town in East Sussex, England
a whiskey distilled mainly from that grain, popular in North America

explanation.surface: A coastal town in England and a spirit share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The same three letters name a Sussex harbour town and a North American grain whiskey.

clue.text: Clean side of window by tree

indicators.note: side of picks one edge of the word window, here its first letter

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Cleaning one side of the window next to a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link putting the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash something is to clean it with water.

clue.text: Recall of lad and lout

indicators.note: recall can mean calling back, so the word for lad is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: Remembering a boy who was a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a rude, aggressive young man, a lout.

clue.text: Coward is cast ready to tremble about first sign of conflict

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the next piece
trembling shakes things up, so the letters of cast and ready are jumbled
the first sign of a word is its initial letter, here of conflict

explanation.surface: A timid person, made ready to shake at the start of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tremble' makes SCAREDYAT, and 'about' wraps it round C from 'conflict'; 'is' is a link. The hyphenated childish insult is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish name for a timid person is a synonym for a coward.

clue.text: I must ache badly after onset of regular pains

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters come behind the next piece
the onset of a word is its first letter, here of regular
badly here means in a disordered way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains of aching terribly following the start of routine pains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' gives HEUMATICS, placed 'after' R from 'regular'. The plural-looking word is an informal British name for rheumatic aches.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for aches in joints and muscles, the pains of rheumatism.

clue.text: Origin of disaster studied completely in a dire way

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter, here of disaster

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
fully means completely

explanation.surface: The cause of the catastrophe was examined thoroughly, in a terrible fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadfully means terribly or awfully, so done in a dire way.

clue.text: List of duties in area to remain on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters are inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A schedule of tasks for those staying in an area, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run, which the draft left unnamed: ATOR sits in areA TO Remain, and 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule saying who does which task and when, a list of duties.

clue.text: Made a bid with amazing fee for gold finally

indicators.note: amazing suggests something astonishing, so the letters are turned around and rearranged
finally picks the last letter, here of gold

explanation.surface: Someone bid with a remarkable price for gold in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' rearranges FEE FOR into OFFERE, then 'finally' adds D from 'gold'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have offered a price is to have made a bid at auction.

clue.text: Journalist enthralled by smart language

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: swish means smart or fashionable
ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for an editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter captivated by a stylish tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The official language of Sweden, spoken by Scandinavians.

clue.text: Restaurant maybe supported by a state

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece lies underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: an Indian is a British term for a curry restaurant, and maybe flags it as an example

explanation.surface: A restaurant, perhaps, held up by a single letter, or a state.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'an Indian' is everyday shorthand for an Indian restaurant or takeaway meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a state of the Midwestern United States.

clue.text: Go away forgetting first sign of ruinous trick

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving something out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: scram is a slang command meaning go away

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter, here of ruinous

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave forgets the warning of a ruinous fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' removes R ('first sign of ruinous') from SCRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme, a confidence trick.

clue.text: Food from abroad cooked by exotic baker with book

parts.note: food that is done is cooked through

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Foreign food made by a foreign baker, with a recipe book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges BAKER into RKEBA; 'by' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This Turkish dish of spit-roasted meat is foreign food that has become a takeaway staple.

clue.text: Drink, one consumed by two Kings

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed by, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king and R stands for Rex, Latin for king
I is the roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drink, one swallowed by a pair of monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is a French aperitif of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur.

clue.text: Man providing a lift at regular intervals

indicators.note: at regular intervals takes every other letter, here of lift

explanation.surface: A man offering someone a ride every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at regular intervals' takes L and F from 'lift'; 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alf is a short form of Alfred, a man's name, and crosswords treat any name as a man.

clue.text: Wine, nothing less, constituting drink in local?

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Pinot is a wine grape and the wine made from it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Wine, without nothing in it, makes up a drink at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub; the question mark admits the definition is an example. 'constituting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint of beer is the classic drink ordered in a British pub.

clue.text: Academic institution found shortly in middle of suburbs

definitions.text: Academic institution found shortly in middle of suburbs

parts.words: Academic institution found shortly in middle of suburbs
parts.note: the place of learning, abbreviated to one letter, sits at the centre of the word suburbs

explanation.surface: A college has been built in the heart of the suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: No wordplay builds the letters: the standard abbreviation U for this institution is the central letter of 'suburbs', and 'shortly' signals the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A university is a place of higher learning, an academic institution.

clue.text: Birds found by Uncle covering face

indicators.note: covering a face hides its front, so the opening letter is lost

parts.note: Uncle Remus is the fictional narrator of the Br'er Rabbit folk tales

explanation.surface: Birds discovered by an uncle hiding his face.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Remus is the storyteller of Joel Chandler Harris's American folk tales; 'covering face' drops his first letter R. 'found by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Large flightless Australian birds, plural like the clue.

clue.text: By the sound of it, longed for a group of players

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is judged on how it is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to have sighed for something is to have longed for it

explanation.surface: Apparently someone yearned for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team, a group of players in a sport.

clue.text: Unkind clerk troubled holding firearm in submission to authority?

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps another inside it
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of unkind clerk are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a gun is a firearm

explanation.surface: A nasty, disturbed office worker with a gun forcing people to obey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' gives KNUCKLINDER, and 'holding' wraps it round the firearm; the question mark flags the phrasal verb as a playful reading of submission.
explanation.definitionFit: Knuckling under means yielding or giving in, so submitting to authority.
